audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gives Ryze Level 1 and Level 6 while every why-line on those rows describes Warwick winning them, and the already-audited mirror has Warwick winning stages 1-5.
audit.why: Warwick wins 55.05% over 396 games. Ryze has no dash or blink; Level 6 is Warwick's biggest swing, not Ryze's, because Realm Warp is a portal, not an escape from a point-and-click suppression.
audit.corrected: Warwick L1-L6 and first item... aligned to the mirror: Warwick, Warwick, Warwick, Warwick, Warwick, Skill, Skill, with ratings raised at 6 and trimmed on the item rows where Ryze's scaling arrives.

audit.whatIsWrong: The item-stage rows claim Warwick simply keeps winning; nothing states where Ryze's mana/AP scaling actually starts pushing back.
audit.why: Warwick's spikes are level 6 (Infinite Duress, 110s at rank 1) and Blade of the Ruined King; Ryze's is stacked bonus mana feeding his passive. The two meet around the item stages, which is a skill window, not a Warwick stage.
audit.corrected: whys[5] and whys[6] rewritten to say he fights back with items while Warwick still catches him when Rune Prison is down.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1].text asserts Infinite Duress 'channels through his Rune Prison (W) root attempt'.
audit.why: Whether a root interrupts Warwick's suppression is not in Riot's text and the kit's 'channel — any CC cancels it' flag is a derived flag, not a statement about roots specifically. The verifiable facts are: Rune Prison is 615 range, roots only with Flux applied, and Ryze has no dash or blink to break a 1.5s suppression.
audit.corrected: Spike rewritten to the verified facts — no mobility, 1.5s suppression, only Flash or the 615-range W as an answer.

audit.whatIsWrong: diff/diffRating call this TRICKY 7.5/10 against a 55.05% win rate and a chart Warwick now owns.
audit.why: The rating drove players to play the lane passively against a champion with no escape.
audit.corrected: FAV, 6/10, with the two prose lines that quote the number updated in the same pass.

edits.before: With items he's still mobility-less — your R and Blood Hunt run him down.
edits.after: Mana-stacked Ryze fights back with items; you still catch him with R.

edits.before: Even late he can't escape your all-in in lane whenever his W is on cooldown.
edits.after: Even late you catch him when Rune Prison (W) is down; grouped, he scales.

edits.before: Infinite Duress channels through his Rune Prison (W) root attempt if you ult first; land R and he has no dash or blink to escape you.
edits.after: Ryze has no dash or blink: land Infinite Duress and he is suppressed 1.5s with only Flash or his 615-range W to answer you.

edits.before: Overall difficulty: 7.5/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Rune Prison and how disciplined your pattern is.
edits.after: Overall difficulty: 6/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Rune Prison (11s) and how disciplined your pattern is.

edits.before: Tricky matchup — difficulty 7.5/10, Ryze carry threat 8.5/10.
edits.after: Favourable matchup — difficulty 6/10, Ryze carry threat 8.5/10.

notes: Not asserted, per the brief's rule on unknowns: whether Rune Prison's root (or the Flux-less slow) interrupts Infinite Duress. The kit's 'channel — any CC cancels it' flag on Warwick's R is derived, and Riot's description says only that he leaps and suppresses. Recorded in unverified rather than written to the page. Chart aligned to the already-audited ryze__warwick mirror (Warwick x5, then Skill, Skill), which also matches the 55.05% win rate.
